Login (erwin/erwin123) works; core reads work; form-template PDF/PNG previews return valid content; concurrency test PASSED — 8 heavy PDF renders in flight did NOT block 12 concurrent /auth/me calls (light p95=2.05s, max=2.13s vs heavy ~2.5s), confirming asyncio.to_thread offload works. critical_code_review_comments: asyncio.to_thread wrapping of render_excel_template / _xlsx_to_pdf / _render_pdf / pdf_page_meta / pdf_page_png in excel_templates, form_templates, qc, nonconformance, bom routers is correct and effective — event loop is no longer blocked (see concurrency numbers). Consider capping the default threadpool (asyncio default is min(32, cpu+4)) via a bounded executor if LibreOffice/PyMuPDF memory usage becomes an issue under real load.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Auth is cookie-based (login returns user obj + Set-Cookie; no access_token in body). Use requests.Session() and login first, then all subsequent requests share cookies. Concurrency validated: form-template preview is a good heavy endpoint (~2.5s) to test event-loop responsiveness. Excel-template PDF endpoints exist but no xlsx templates seeded, so those preview tests skip — main agent can upload a test .xlsx to /api/excel-templates to enable them if needed.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bug found. Concurrency fix behaves as intended: light requests responded within 2.13s max while 8 heavy PDF renders (~2.5s each) ran concurrently in the threadpool. Prior to the fix, sync render calls would have serialized all requests on the event loop and light /auth/me would have queued for many seconds.
